description: Conformance vectors for the CURRENT APMap contract. Every valid vector must be accepted by the one schema under schema/ AND pass every semantic rule; every invalid one must be rejected by the schema, and rejected for the reason recorded here rather than incidentally; every semantic_invalid one PASSES the schema and must be refused by a conforming semantic validator for exactly the SEM-* rule it names. A document declaring a deprecated version is not a vector here at all — it is validated against its own frozen contract and promoted, and deprecated/1.0/one-zero-document.apmap, deprecated/1.1/one-one-document.apmap, deprecated/1.2/one-two-document.apmap and deprecated/1.3/one-three-document.apmap are the fixtures for that.

valid.exercises: derived_from kind 'operation' on a brush, with every optional member present: operation, ordinal, replaces, intent. Inherited from 1.1 and still current.
derived_from kind 'operation' carrying nothing but kind and operation_id — the documented minimum.
operation provenance on all three object kinds at once: entity, brush, and face, the face using the free-form metadata member.
broken: true on a brush item.
broken: false written explicitly. Absent means false, but a producer that writes it is not in error.
groups at their simplest: one group named 'Entrance Columns' over two brushes, and no `source` — which is what every group a user makes by hand looks like.
one group holding all three member kinds at once — entity, brush and face — each through its own kind-specific id field.

two groups in one document, deliberately sharing the visible name 'Group 1'. The name is a label; identity is group_id, and duplicates are legal. Its 1.3 ancestor put brush brs_cube00000000a1 and that brush's own face in one group — a containment fault (SEM-G-5) the schema cannot see and the 1.3 corpus still carries, frozen. This descendant names a face of the OTHER brush, so it is valid under every rule.

1.3's addition: the same group carrying source { kind: 'prefab', prefab_id }, the durable record that it was created by placing a prefab. The identity is the library's, so it holds slashes and no APMap prefix; nothing else about the prefab — no screenshot, no URL, no title, no owner — is in the document.

a document declaring the current version with no group and no `authorship`. `groups` is required of a current writer, so the empty array is what 'no groups' looks like; `authorship` is optional, and its absence is what 'nobody recorded who made this' looks like — which is exactly what a promoted legacy document says.

1.4's relaxation: a persisted group with ONE member. 1.3 refused this exact document (it is still under deprecated/1.3/test-vectors/invalid/); 1.4 accepts it, because a CUT or a removal can leave a real group holding one brush.
the CUT result shape the relaxation exists for: two groups, 'Cut-out' and 'Remainder', each holding exactly one brush — no sliver invented to reach a count.
1.4's `group` member arm: 'Entrance' holds the group 'Columns' (two brushes) and two loose brushes. Expanding 'Entrance' reaches all four brushes, each once.
three levels — 'Building' ⊃ 'Entrance' ⊃ 'Columns' — with a one-member middle group and an entity at the top. Declaration order is not nesting order: a child may be declared after its parent.

every `authorship` member at once, pinned for exact round-trip: apostrophes, double quotes, an ampersand, an em dash, non-ASCII Latin and CJK names, a copyright notice with a line break and a licence with a blank line and a TAB. A reader that trims, normalizes or re-punctuates any of it changed the author's words.

the three states side by side: `author` is the empty string (somebody deliberately recorded no author), `license` holds text, and `copyright_notice` is ABSENT (unknown). A consumer must keep all three distinct and must not fill the absent one.

invalid.violation: derived_from kind 'rewrite' matches none of the five defined kinds, so the oneOf matches nothing. A new provenance kind is a schema change, never a producer's invention.
kind 'operation' without operation_id. The operation that produced the object is the one member beyond kind that is always required; without it the record names no cause.

kind 'operation' carrying an undeclared member 'authorized'. additionalProperties is false, so a producer cannot introduce a field a consumer might read as permission. Annotation goes in intent or metadata, and neither authorizes anything.
broken is the string "true", not a boolean. There are two states and absence is the third spelling of false; a truthy string is none of them.

apmap_version "999.999" is not a version this schema defines. An unknown FUTURE version is refused rather than guessed at. The sentinel is deliberately far outside the numbering: this vector used to declare the next unreleased minor, and promoting that minor turned the vector into a valid document overnight.

the document declares the current version and omits `groups`. A current writer always emits the member; an absent one is indistinguishable from a producer that does not know groups exist, and 'no groups' must be sayable.
a name of three spaces. The name is what a user reads in the Groups list, so it must be non-empty after trimming; `pattern: \S` is how the schema says 'at least one non-whitespace character'.
group_id 'group_entrance0001' uses the wrong prefix. Every APMap id kind is distinguishable from its prefix alone; `grp_` is the group's.

a member declaring kind 'entity' whose entity_id holds a brush id. The union is discriminated on kind and each arm names its own id field, so a mismatched reference fails at the contract rather than later, at resolution.
a member carrying a generic `object_id` instead of the kind's own field. One untyped id field is exactly what the discriminated union exists to prevent.
a member carrying an undeclared member 'label'. additionalProperties is false: a member is a reference and nothing else, and per-member editor state is not map truth.
the same brush listed twice in one group. Membership is a set; a duplicate says nothing new and would make member counts lie.

source.prefab_id is the empty string. Provenance that names nothing is worse than no provenance: it makes the group claim an origin no reader can ever resolve, and the tag it drives would be permanently unexplainable.

source.kind 'annotation' is not the one origin 1.3 defines. A new kind of origin is a schema change, never a producer's invention — a consumer meeting an unknown one could only guess what the group's history was.

source carrying an undeclared member 'preview_image_url'. additionalProperties is false, and this is the exact member the contract exists to keep out: the screenshot belongs to the prefab library, which owns it, can revoke it and can re-render it. A URL copied into the map would be a stale, unauthenticated second copy of somebody else's asset.
a group with NO member. 1.4 lowered the minimum to one, not to zero: an empty group is a name over nothing, and the editor dissolves a group in the same transaction that removed its last member.
a member declaring kind 'group' whose group_id holds a brush id. The group arm is discriminated like every other: its id must be a `grp_` id.
`authorship: {}`. 'Nothing recorded' has exactly one spelling — omit the member — so that two writers of the same document emit the same bytes.

`authorship` carrying an undeclared member 'uploader'. The object is closed, and this is the member it exists to keep out: who uploaded or saved a file is an account fact, not authorship, and the two must never share a field.
`author` is an array. It is one human-readable line; several contributors are written the way the author writes them, and a structured contributor list belongs in a namespaced extension.
`author` is 257 characters; the bound is 256 (counted in Unicode code points).
`author` contains a line break. It is a single line; the notice and the licence may span lines, the author may not.
`license` contains U+0007 BEL. LF and TAB are the only control characters a multi-line member may hold.
`copyright_notice` uses a CRLF line break. Line breaks are LF (SER-2); an editor converts at input, and the document never carries a CR.
`license` is 4097 characters; the bound is 4096. Longer licence wording belongs beside the map, referenced by name.

semantic_invalid.violation: a group lists itself as a member — the shortest cycle. Expansion would never terminate, and 'a group of itself' names nothing.
Alpha contains Beta and Beta contains Alpha: a cycle of length two. Each group has exactly one parent, so SEM-G-4 alone does not catch it.
Alpha ⊃ Beta ⊃ Gamma ⊃ Alpha: a cycle of length three, found only by following the graph.
the group 'Columns' is a direct member of both 'Entrance' and 'Courtyard'. A group has at most one parent, exactly as an object is a direct member of at most one group.
a `group` member names grp_nowhere0000001, which no group in the document declares.
a `brush` member names brs_cube00000000e5, which no entity in the document owns.
brush brs_cube00000000a1 is a direct member of two groups.
two groups declare the same group_id; a reference to it would resolve to two groups, which is to say to neither.

'Entrance' holds brush a1 directly and, through its child 'Columns', a1's own face. The expansion of 'Entrance' would name the same geometry twice; 1.4 applies containment normalization across the nesting, not only within one member list.
a chain of 33 nested groups; 32 is the deepest a document may nest. The bound is what lets every reader traverse without recursion limits and every UI draw the tree.
`author` ends in the escape \ud83d with no low surrogate after it. That is not Unicode text; a reader must refuse it rather than re-emit it as U+FFFD, which would silently change the author's words.
